text: As the train neared Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> Jack Potter grew more and more uneasy. <break time="0.8s" /> For he had married. <break time="0.8s" /> Without consulting the town. <break time="0.8s" /> Of which he was the marshal. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a man. <break time="0.8s" /> Known, liked, and feared. <break time="0.8s" /> In his corner of the West. <break time="0.8s" /> And to marry secretly. <break time="0.8s" /> Seemed to him an extraordinary crime. <break time="0.8s" /> Against the town. <break time="0.8s" /> He knew full well. <break time="0.8s" /> That his marriage was an important thing. <break time="0.8s" /> To his town. <break time="0.8s" /> An event. <break time="0.8s" /> Which only the burning of the new hotel could exceed. <break time="0.8s" /> He had often thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Of sending them a telegram. <break time="0.8s" /> But a new cowardice had come upon him. <break time="0.8s" /> And now he dreaded the moment of arrival. <break time="0.8s" /> He planned to hurry with her. <break time="0.8s" /> From the station to his house. <break time="0.8s" /> And to stay away from the citizens. <break time="0.8s" /> Until their excitement had worn off a little. <break time="0.8s" /> What is worrying you, Jack. <break time="0.8s" /> She asked. <break time="0.8s" /> And he laughed and answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was only thinking of Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> And she flushed in comprehension. <break time="0.8s" /> A sense of mutual guilt. <break time="0.8s" /> Invaded their minds. <break time="0.8s" /> And developed a finer tenderness. <break time="0.8s" /> And they looked at each other. <break time="0.8s" /> With eyes softly aglow. <break time="0.8s" /> When the train stopped at Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> Potter gripped his wifes arm. <break time="0.8s" /> Firmly to his side. <break time="0.8s" /> And they hurried away together. <break time="0.8s" /> Before the station agent could reach them.
